content:
Branding not only shapes customer relationships, but it also affects the organizational culture. To be successful, brand managers must possess a proven, diverse range of skills. Consider how a great brand manager can boost a brand and strengthen the company with some core competencies. 

Your brand manager plays an instrumental role in building enduring perceptions of your business and guiding your brand’s growth, whether they operate in-house or at a third-party agency.

Core Attributes

Key personal attributes for a successful brand manager include 

  • Brand awareness 
  • Determination and perseverance
  • Relationship management skills
  • A strong focus on results
  • A high degree of business acumen

The objective is to maintain brand integrity across all types of products and communications and to continuously develop positive brand perception among your target audience. 

Here are the 9 most important skills a brand manager should bring to a team.

Relationship Management

Brand management and collaboration start within the organization. When you work through various divisions and collaborate with diverse teams, the capacity to maintain partnerships, coordinate with corporate processes, and facilitate meaningful brand association internally is necessary. 

Simply placed, a brand manager must act as the gatekeeper of the company’s products and services. This suggests that everybody knows and can leverage brand marketing and messaging.  More specifically, when engaging with other departments and staff, it involves showing a sincere excitement and passion for the brand, and championing it at any level. 

Furthermore, brand managers need to have a clear knowledge of their clients and vendors,  including the ability to interpret market analysis and consumer research.

Good Communication 

Brand managers communicate with a wide range of people, including their staff, their team members, and the clients.  To be successful, they should be able to communicate ideas, expectations, and requests clearly and effectively. Moreover, they should excel in both organizational and interpersonal communication, which means they must be able to share information in both large groups and one-on-one conversations. 

Successful brand managers collaborate through a wide variety of teams and push for company-wide collaboration on diverse projects. 

Communication skills are present during a speech, presentation, day-to-day talk, elevator pitches to executives, or between you and a peer. Therefore, each engagement is important to present the core values of Personal Brand in a positive light.

Analytical Thinking and Creative Storytelling 

Top-notch storytelling and strategic creative thinking are both sought-after attributes by brand managers. You ought to be able to gather information from the data and use it to tell a story that makes the brand irresistible to consumers. 

Excellent writing and design skills are nice to have, but it’s more essential to be able to balance creativity and strategy and transition smoothly from research and facts to creativity in communication. Successful brand marketers also think analytically about diversifying engagement approaches through the whole consumer experience.

Innovative and Strategic Thinking

Brand managers must be both strategic and creative. They should move discreetly between research and facts towards communication creativity, which requires them to be analytical, verbal, creative and visual. 

Innovation is important in every field, but innovative and better business ideas are pushing business in the corporate and marketing environment. Hence, a successful brand manager must incorporate these and be an innovator to attract, retain, and expand the customer base. 

Also being able to formulate a marketing plan that is compatible with the broader corporate strategy and ‘thinking’ creatively about all areas of marketing is something that a marketer needs to possess. Therefore, a brand manager should have a good understanding of market dynamics, to be able to establish a tailored marketing strategy, and to achieve higher business objectives.

Adaptability

The fundamental quality that brand managers require is the opportunity to be agile even though it appears challenging.  Due to potential market changes, the only path ahead for a brand is through adaptation. If it’s by some sort of new concept or effective marketing, the manager needs to be able to build new possibilities without neglecting the core brand ideas. It is also important to have the flexibility to use social media correctly for branding campaigns. Finally, understanding the brand conversations on these various channels is crucial and a policy needs to be adapted as these trends evolve.

Since we live in a world where information can be accessed from anywhere and at any time, consumers have multichannel access to brands. The way we perceive brands and the relationship we have with them is constantly evolving. Therefore, brand managers must adapt and evolve along with them.

In-Depth Knowledge of Marketing Best Practices

“While applying a brand name to a product/service, brand managers are required to follow certain principles, like the name of the product should be simple to remember, easy to pronounce, highly recognizable and easily and accurately translated into all languages of the target consumer market. They should be aware of the latest trends in the market and must come up with ideas for new packaging designs, including shape, size, colors, fonts, and imagery. 

A brand manager is responsible for developing new products according to the demands of the consumer. And for this, they coordinate with various other sections and departments of production, R&D, advertising, sales, promotion, marketing research, purchasing, distribution, package development, and finance, etc. A brand manager should be able to present the product’s benefit as well as the company’s image in the market and look superior as compared to other brands in the market. Now online brand management, known as e-branding, is also becoming popular through social networking sites and blogs.

Effective Targeting

A good marketer has made the leap of faith and accepted that fewer target consumers will deliver a better overall result. Usually, that means stepping back from the segmentation and only going after 10% or 20% of the potential market. Tight target segments mean the marketing has a chance to succeed. Too many marketers lose faith at this stage and end up targeting pretty much everyone.

“Which leads nicely to the next feature of a great marketer: being entirely comfortable devoting time and marketing money to excluding the wrong kinds of consumers from your brand. Most marketers, when asked, still don’t know the difference between marketing and sales. Marketing is as much about stopping the wrong people from buying a product as ensuring that the right ones do. Usually, the majority of potential consumers in any market will cost you money if you serve them. A good marketer knows this and uses his or her skills to ensure they are avoided.” 

Creativity

“You can’t use up creativity. The more you use the more you have.” – Maya Angelou

Marketing is in many ways a creative endeavor. Marketing managers should be able to develop unique and interesting ways to sell products or promote the brand. This involves the ability to come up with original ideas and innovate ways to make them a reality. To be successful in the industry, marketing managers must be able to capture and hold their audience’s attention.

Creative skills for a marketing manager often involve 

  • Brainstorming ideas with graphic designers and artists
  • Evaluating the aesthetic appeal of marketing materials
  • Devising creative methods for promoting and distributing products
  • Planning and executing promotional events and activities

Creative teams with strategic targets innovate the best brands. However, it is fair to say that too much structuring of these creatives hampers their innovation. Because of this, effective brand managers know to implement strategies that encourage creativity instead of restricting it.

One of the things that separate good and great brand managers is the ability to find the right balance between structure and innovation within their creative strategies. These processes should give their creative teams the chance to stay focused while boosting progress in fulfilling brand objectives. The key to this is a combination of prior planning and periodic intervention when necessary.

A good brand manager will have an understanding of when they should reiterate branding goals that encourage team creativity.

Social Media Savvy

In the digital age, what makes a good brand manager? Must-have skills now include social media savvy, as well as the ability to leverage digital marketing tools and technology. 

A brand manager knows how to leverage digital marketing expertise to excel in the social arena. Set your brand apart from the competition by telling the story of the company and its mission with fervor through social media channels. Define what the company stands for, and let it resonate in every post and picture shared. Use vivid images that incorporate brand colors, and develop a catchy tagline to add a unique, memorable touch.

Using social media tools to listen to the conversations surrounding your brand is key. Brand managers seek honest feedback from customers and social media followers to make progressive changes online and offline. If the website or social media strategy is not reaching the target audience, revamp the social media strategy, and make improvements until you note positive changes.

The quest to establish and maintain a reputable business brand never ends as long as the company exists. If you apply exceptional branding and marketing techniques, you can build greater visibility in your market and gain the trust and allegiance of consumers. Businesses continue to look to brilliant brand managers for direction, and those who know how to achieve exceptional results remain in demand.

title: AI in Management: Boosting Team Performance
excerpt: Managers today face a fast-changing workplace, and AI is a powerful new ally. Imagine having an assistant who never sleeps and helps you make decisions. AI in management means using smart tools to automate tasks and analyze data. This frees up leaders to focus on strategy, creativity, and personal interactions with their team. Benefits of […]
content:
Managers today face a fast-changing workplace, and AI is a powerful new ally. Imagine having an assistant who never sleeps and helps you make decisions. AI in management means using smart tools to automate tasks and analyze data. This frees up leaders to focus on strategy, creativity, and personal interactions with their team.

Benefits of AI in Management

Artificial Intelligence can help managers make data-driven decisions. By analyzing large amounts of information, AI tools spot trends and suggest solutions. For example, an AI tool might forecast sales or team productivity, so you can plan better and avoid surprises. AI in management also streamlines routine work like scheduling or reporting. When AI handles these tasks accurately and quickly, your team can use their time for creative problem-solving and collaboration. This boosts overall productivity and engagement.

Using AI to Improve Team Performance

When managers use AI responsibly, teams can perform at their best. AI-driven analytics track progress on projects and highlight areas where people might need support or training. For example, an AI tool can identify if someone is overloaded or help simplify complex data. When people get timely feedback and help, trust and efficiency grow. These AI tools keep your team aligned and motivated. Importantly, AI in management should not replace personal connections. Instead, it should enhance them. For instance, AI can help by handling routine tasks or suggesting improvements, freeing you to engage more personally with your team.

Embracing AI Carefully

It’s crucial to remember that AI is a tool, not a boss. Good managers introduce AI gradually and train the team on it. Transparency about how AI is used builds trust. Address any privacy or bias concerns openly. AI in management offers big gains, but it works best when paired with clear human values. Staying curious and learning about AI keeps managers ahead.

In summary, AI in management is reshaping the leader’s role. It handles routine work and provides insights, letting managers focus on people and strategy. By embracing AI thoughtfully, teams can be more productive, satisfied, and ready for the future. If you’re managing a team now, explore one AI tool and see how it can help: your team may surprise you. For more insights, check out more management blogs on Businessleader Insights.

title: AI-Powered Customer Service: Revolutionizing User Experience
excerpt: In today’s digitally-driven era, businesses are constantly seeking innovative ways to enhance customer satisfaction. One such groundbreaking solution is AI-powered customer service, a technology that’s reshaping user experience and support services across industries. This transformative approach not only streamlines processes but also elevates customer interactions to unprecedented levels. Personalized Interactions Through AI AI-powered customer service […]
content:
In today’s digitally-driven era, businesses are constantly seeking innovative ways to enhance customer satisfaction. One such groundbreaking solution is AI-powered customer service, a technology that’s reshaping user experience and support services across industries. This transformative approach not only streamlines processes but also elevates customer interactions to unprecedented levels.

Personalized Interactions Through AI

AI-powered customer service introduces a new paradigm where interactions are personalized and tailored to individual needs. By leveraging machine learning algorithms, AI systems analyze vast amounts of customer data in real time, allowing companies to understand preferences, behaviors, and pain points. This knowledge enables the delivery of customized support, offering solutions aligned with specific customer needs promptly.

24/7 Availability and Instantaneous Responses

Unlike traditional customer service, AI-powered systems operate round the clock. This non-stop availability ensures that customers receive support whenever they require it, irrespective of time zones or holidays. Furthermore, the instantaneous nature of AI-driven responses significantly reduces wait times, contributing to a seamless and efficient user experience.

Enhanced Efficiency and Scalability

AI-powered systems excel in handling repetitive tasks and inquiries. By automating routine processes, these systems free up human agents to focus on more complex issues that require empathy and critical thinking. Moreover, as businesses expand, AI systems effortlessly scale to accommodate increased customer demands without compromising quality.

Natural Language Processing (NLP) for Superior Communication

With advancements in natural language processing, AI-enabled chatbots and virtual assistants can comprehend and respond to natural language queries. This capability enables fluid and human-like conversations, enhancing the overall customer experience. By understanding context and intent, these AI systems can provide accurate information and resolutions swiftly.

Data-Driven Insights for Proactive Support

The wealth of data processed by AI systems provides invaluable insights into customer behavior and trends. By analyzing this data, businesses can anticipate potential issues and proactively address them, offering preemptive solutions before customers even realize they have a problem. This proactive approach not only prevents escalations but also fosters stronger customer loyalty.

Improved Decision Making with Predictive Analytics

AI empowers businesses with predictive analytics, enabling them to forecast future customer needs and behaviors. By analyzing historical data, AI algorithms can predict trends, enabling companies to make informed decisions regarding product development, marketing strategies, and service improvements. This foresight helps in staying ahead of customer expectations and market changes.

Human-AI Collaboration: The Perfect Blend

While AI-powered customer service offers numerous benefits, the human touch remains indispensable. Integrating AI with human agents creates a symbiotic relationship where AI handles routine tasks and data analysis while humans provide empathy, creativity, and complex issue resolution. This blend ensures a comprehensive and empathetic customer service experience.

Challenges and Ethical Considerations

Implementing AI in customer service isn’t devoid of challenges. Ensuring data privacy, maintaining transparency in AI decision-making processes, and addressing biases in algorithms are crucial ethical considerations. Balancing technological advancements with ethical practices is essential to build trust and ensure responsible AI deployment.

Future Prospects and Continuous Innovation

The landscape of AI-powered customer service is continuously evolving. Advancements in AI, including the integration of voice AI, augmented reality, and predictive modeling, promise even more enhanced user experiences. The future holds potential for more sophisticated AI systems that can handle complex queries with human-like understanding and emotional intelligence.

Conclusion: Transforming Customer Service Dynamics

AI-powered customer service represents a paradigm shift in how businesses engage with their customers. By offering personalized, efficient, and proactive support, AI systems elevate user experiences while optimizing operational efficiency. As technology evolves, the collaboration between AI and human agents will continue to redefine customer service, ensuring seamless interactions and unparalleled support for users worldwide.

title: AI-Powered Thought Leadership: Can Machines Help Shape Human Opinion?
excerpt: In a time where computers recommend what we read, watch, and even consider, an intriguing query is circulating: Is it possible for AI to Direct Thought? It’s not as science fiction as it seems. AI is already assisting C-suite executives with writing opinion pieces, summarizing studies, and even ghost-writing social media postings. Does that suggest, […]
content:
In a time where computers recommend what we read, watch, and even consider, an intriguing query is circulating:

Is it possible for AI to Direct Thought?

It’s not as science fiction as it seems. AI is already assisting C-suite executives with writing opinion pieces, summarizing studies, and even ghost-writing social media postings. Does that suggest, however, that AI is influencing human opinion or merely assisting those who hold it?

Let’s examine this.

What Exactly Is Thought Leadership?

Fundamentally, thought leadership is about persuading people with knowledge, skill, and a genuine viewpoint. It’s an incredibly human undertaking. Thought leaders are followed not only for their knowledge but also for their opinions. Their principles, voice, and vision are all important.

Therefore, when we discuss AI in this context, we are enhancing thought leaders rather than replacing them.

How AI Is Getting into the Discussion

Professionals are now benefiting from AI tools:

• Real-time trend analysis of the industry
• Creation of content drafts that inspire fresh concepts
• Customization of messaging for audiences
• Identification of discourse gaps

Imagine it as an extremely competent helper who is always available and has been reading everything, everywhere, at once.

The thinking isn’t being done by the machine. For the human to think more clearly, creatively, and strategically, is performing the processing—the heavy lifting.

Benefits Include Quickness, Scale, and Intelligence

AI offers several significant benefits.

Speed: An AI tool can save hours of human research by sorting through thousands of articles in a matter of seconds.

Scale: Previously, thought leadership was restricted to white papers and speeches. AI has made it simple to repackage a single idea into blogs, tweets, videos, and emails.

Smarts: By identifying patterns that people would overlook, natural language models can reveal subtle insights.

The goal is to elevate the floor so that leaders may concentrate on higher-level thinking, not to dumb things down.

The Dangers of Trust and Authenticity

There is a flip side, though. It gets more difficult to determine who said what in increasingly polished and widely distributed AI-generated content.

Will your followers still believe you if they discover that 90% of your posts are automated?

Authenticity is the key to thought leadership’s strength. Therefore, your ultimate ideas, opinions, and voice should remain yours even if AI assists with content drafting. Machines can inform your view, but they shouldn’t take its place.

The Crucial Question – Who Is Developing the Concepts?

Here’s the main idea: Being a thought leader is more than just producing results. It involves thought. And only humans are still capable of doing so, at least in a way that is morally righteous, emotionally compelling, and significant.

AI can speed up your journey. It can help you see things more broadly. What about the destination? Humans still make that choice.

Last Remark

Can machines, then, influence human opinion?

Yes, provided they are used carefully.

The most brilliant minds of the future might not possess superhuman abilities. They will, however, be the ones who discover how to collaborate with technology in a way that enriches rather than replaces their human voice.

Perhaps the most effective leadership is the ability to use new tools without compromising your viewpoint.

title: Analyzing the Impact of Mobile-First Indexing on Digital Marketing Strategies
excerpt: Mobile-first indexing has become a crucial change in the constantly changing digital ecosystem for both search engines and digital marketers. Search engines like Google give preference to mobile versions of websites when indexing and ranking them because mobile devices now make up most of the internet traffic. Digital marketers must modify their approaches to remain […]
content:
Mobile-first indexing has become a crucial change in the constantly changing digital ecosystem for both search engines and digital marketers. Search engines like Google give preference to mobile versions of websites when indexing and ranking them because mobile devices now make up most of the internet traffic. Digital marketers must modify their approaches to remain efficient and competitive during this shift. We will discuss how digital marketing strategies are affected by mobile-first indexing in this blog post, along with actions you can do to adjust to this new reality.

Mobile-First Indexing: What Is It?

Google prioritizes indexing and ranking websites based mostly on their mobile form; a practice known as mobile-first indexing. The growing number of people using mobile devices to access the web was the driving force behind this change. Search engine rankings for websites that are not mobile-friendly can drop, which can affect their exposure and visitors.

The Significance of Mobile-First Indexing

An Increase in Mobile Traffic: Since mobile users now surpass desktop users, it’s imperative to make sure your website works well on mobile devices if you want to connect with them.

Search Engine Rankings: Mobile-friendly websites are now given priority by Google’s algorithm. Lower search rankings for a website that doesn’t accommodate mobile visitors may result in less organic traffic.

User Experience: The significance of a smooth user experience on mobile devices is highlighted by mobile-first indexing. Increased engagement and conversions can result from a mobile site that is both user-friendly and responsive.

Effect on Online Marketing Techniques

Responsive Design: To ensure that websites adjust to different screen sizes and devices, responsive design strategies should be used. This strategy complies with Google’s mobile-first indexing policy while also enhancing user experience.

Optimizing Page Speed: Users on mobile devices anticipate pages to load quickly. Reduced search ranks and increased bounce rates might result from slow load times. Page speed can be improved by using strategies like lazy loading and image optimization.

Content Strategy: Material needs to be mobile-friendly. This entails producing succinct, captivating content that loads rapidly and reads well on small displays. Give priority to formats that are easy on mobile devices, like concise paragraphs, bullet points, and distinct headers.

Conclusion

The practice of mobile-first indexing signifies a substantial change in the way search engines assess and prioritize webpages. Businesses need to emphasize mobile optimization and modify their tactics appropriately if they want to stay ahead of the curve in the world of digital marketing.

title: Beyond NPS: Next-Gen Metrics That Truly Measure Customer Success
excerpt: For many years, Net Promoter Score (NPS) has been the most reliable metric for gauging customer performance. Even though NPS offers insightful data on customer happiness and loyalty, it frequently fails to fully capture the range of customer experiences and business impact. Organizations must develop a more comprehensive strategy to gauge success in today’s customer-centric […]
content:
For many years, Net Promoter Score (NPS) has been the most reliable metric for gauging customer performance. Even though NPS offers insightful data on customer happiness and loyalty, it frequently fails to fully capture the range of customer experiences and business impact. Organizations must develop a more comprehensive strategy to gauge success in today’s customer-centric world. These next-generation measures provide more in-depth, useful information than NPS.

1. Customer Effort Score
Consumers appreciate the ease of use. CES gauges how simple or complex a customer’s task is, whether utilizing a feature, buying something, or fixing a problem. A smoother experience is indicated by a lower effort score, which increases loyalty and retention.

2. Health Score for Customers (CHS)
A predictive indicator called the Customer Health Score assesses a customer’s propensity for expansion, attrition, or renewal. It provides an early warning system for possible churn by combining elements like sentiment analysis, customer engagement, support interactions, and product usage.

3. TTV, or Time to Value
TTV calculates the time it takes a consumer to recognize the worth of a good or service. A shorter TTV suggests that clients are meeting their objectives more rapidly, which raises customer satisfaction and the possibility of long-term adoption.

4. Rate of Product Adoption
It’s critical to comprehend how frequently and deeply people interact with your product. By calculating the proportion of users who actively use important features, this statistic assists companies in finding ways to improve user experience and increase engagement.

5. Customer Lifetime Value
The entire revenue a company can anticipate from a single customer over the course of their relationship is predicted by CLV. Strong client retention and successful upselling or cross-selling tactics are indicated by a growing CLV.

6. Rate of Expansion Revenue
This indicator focuses on the money made from current clients through renewals, upgrades, and extra services. Strong product-market fit and efficient customer relationship management are indicated by a high expansion rate.

7. Analysis of Sentiment
Analyzing customer reviews, feedback, and support issues using AI-powered solutions can yield insightful sentiment data. To develop a more complex view of consumer happiness, this qualitative data is used in conjunction with quantitative measurements.

8. Score for Engagement
Engagement scoring considers more than simply logins; it also takes into account how users interact with features, consume content, and communicate with support staff. Better advocacy and retention are frequently correlated with more involvement.

Conclusion

Even if NPS is still a helpful metric, modern customer success necessitates a more thorough approach. Businesses can improve their understanding of customer behavior, foresee problems, and promote long-term success by using next-generation metrics like CES, CHS, and CLV. By adopting these cutting-edge customer success metrics, businesses can make sure they are actively cultivating meaningful relationships and long-term company success in addition to monitoring customer satisfaction.

title: Boosting Employee Morale Amidst Economic Uncertainty
excerpt: When employee morale is low for a lengthy period of time, good leaders provide assistance and time off for relaxation.
content:
Employees have gone through a lot as a result of the pandemic and all of the changes it has brought. The current economic uncertainty is yet another element to consider. High morale, on the other hand, can be the difference between surviving and thriving. This is no simple task given the global health crisis, the economic slump, workforce reductions, remote work, and evolving job duties.  

When employee morale is low for a lengthy period of time, good leaders provide assistance and time off for relaxation. And, as leaders, it’s critical to encourage staff and convince them that the company is on their side, even when circumstances are tough. 

5 Suggestions to Boost Employee Morale 

If morale and engagement are high in your workplace, you can create space for employees to do their best even through challenging times. Here are five ways to maintain employee morale now when it matters more than ever 

Offering Gratitude and Appreciation

Creating a culture of acknowledgment and gratitude in your company is one of the most important aspects of boosting morale. Employees are more encouraged to keep up the good job when they know their efforts are noticed and recognized. A simple thank you note, or even a gift card for employee of the month, as well as public recognition, may go a far way. Make an effort to remember special occasions such as birthdays, marriages, and work anniversaries. Invest in your employees, and you’ll soon see how much high morale can benefit a company.  

Caring for Employees and Recognizing Them

Making employees feel cared for is another factor that might boost morale. This might include offering advantages and bonuses that cater to their specific requirements, such as free yoga lessons or nutritious food. Make it a point to listen to your staff and reassure them that they are not alone. Recognizing and acknowledging employees’ worries and sentiments is possibly the most crucial strategy to keep morale up. 

Providing Work Flexibility

Offering flexibility is also important. Recognize that everyone’s situation is different. Provide work flexibly in the way that suits each employee best, like encouraging a hybrid model, so they can balance work with their lives.  

Establishing Frequent Communication

Communication is arguably the most effective way to boost employee morale. Set up weekly all-company meetings and encourage your people to ask you tough questions ahead of time. Maintaining frequent communication also fosters trust in the organization’s management and leadership. 

Empowering Employees

Encourage and welcome creativity on a regular basis. Include employees that you don’t hear from too often. Employees that are quiet aren’t generally those who don’t have amazing ideas or opinions. Consider establishing a cross-training program where workers may learn from one another and explore other areas/positions within the organization. As a result, institutional knowledge is reinforced, cooperation improves as a result of increased understanding, and possible career progression leads to higher retention. 

Summing Up 

The key to boosting employee morale in the workplace is to make sure they are valued as individuals, not just as tools. This provides people with the trust that, regardless of the state of the economy, your business will treat them fairly and with care. You may create an environment in which people feel noticed, respected, and supported, and in which they can accomplish their best job.

title: Boosting Loyalty: The Proactive Customer Success Strategy
excerpt: In today’s market, waiting for customers to report problems is costing businesses. True sustainable growth does not come from fixing fires but preventing them. Business leaders understand that keeping existing clients is profitable and cost-effective than finding new ones. This financial reality makes adopting a proactive customer success strategy the single most powerful shift your […]
content:
In today’s market, waiting for customers to report problems is costing businesses. True sustainable growth does not come from fixing fires but preventing them. Business leaders understand that keeping existing clients is profitable and cost-effective than finding new ones. This financial reality makes adopting a proactive customer success strategy the single most powerful shift your business can make right now. This approach uses data to expect needs, ensuring your customers realize value faster, stay longer, and spend more.

Why Your Strategy Needs a Proactive Customer Success Strategy

Moving from a support model where teams wait for tickets to a proactive customer success strategy is mandatory for modern profitability. By helping customers before problems happen, we save them time and make things easier. By identifying clients who are showing early signs of decline, perhaps a dip in product usage or limited engagement, you can intervene effectively. Predictive analytics enable this commitment to anticipation, and research shows they increase customer retention by a notable 15–20%. This strategy builds customer loyalty.

Simple Steps for a Proactive Customer Success Strategy

The core of a successful customer success strategy lies in understanding customer health using data. Instead of waiting for a complaint or cancellation, organizations implement an early warning system.

Monitor Usage: Track product adoption metrics. If a key feature remains unused, send a tailored tutorial email or suggest a brief check-in call. For example, if a software company notices a user struggling with a specific feature, the company can send personalized tips instead of waiting for the user to reach out for help. This shows crucial attentiveness and prevents frustration.

Personalized Outreach: Use your data to trigger targeted engagements. This proactive customer success strategy transforms generic mass communication into high-value interactions. By offering help before it’s requested, businesses build stronger relationships and greater trust, which translates into customer retention strategies.

Conclusion

Implementing a proactive customer success strategy is not about providing better service; it is a clear, data-driven path to greater profitability and sustained competitive advantage. By leveraging intelligent data to prevent issues and ensure continued value realization, businesses transform reactive support costs into powerful revenue generation opportunities. Companies that master this strategic shift show lasting customer relationships and increase their likelihood of long-term success.

title: Bowling Under Pressure: What Cricketers Can Teach Us About Managing Workload Before Big Moments
excerpt: It’s the final over—the stadium roars. The batter stares down the pitch. The bowler grips the ball, takes a breath, and charges in. Now imagine you’re not on a cricket field but walking into a high-stakes presentation, a product launch, or a boardroom pitch. The pressure’s real, the stakes are high, and all eyes are […]
content:
It’s the final over—the stadium roars. The batter stares down the pitch. The bowler grips the ball, takes a breath, and charges in.

Now imagine you’re not on a cricket field but walking into a high-stakes presentation, a product launch, or a boardroom pitch. The pressure’s real, the stakes are high, and all eyes are on you.

Whether it’s the World Cup or the workplace, the moments that matter most demand composure, clarity, and preparation. Interestingly, elite cricketers have a few tricks up their sleeve when it comes to managing workload and pressure—strategies that can help all of us perform better in our professional “final overs.”

Let’s break it down.

1. Train Hard, Rest Harder

Top cricketers don’t just train harder—they recover smarter. Managing workload is now a science in cricket, with tools like the Player Load Index helping coaches balance training intensity and rest. Why? Because fatigue kills focus.

Work Takeaway: Don’t cram before a big project or presentation. Plan sprints of productivity balanced with strategic rest—what productivity expert Cal Newport calls deep work, followed by deliberate rest. Burnout will bowl you out before the moment even arrives.

2. Simulate the Pressure

Cricketers often simulate match scenarios during practice to normalise pressure. Think death over training or match simulations with crowd noise.

Work Takeaway: Practice a keynote in front of colleagues. Rehearse tough conversations. Simulate Q&A sessions. When managing workload, the more real it feels, the more composed you’ll be when the moment comes.

3. Control the Controllables

Cricketers learn to control what they can—line, length, breath—not the pitch conditions or crowd noise.

Work Takeaway: Before your big moment, ask: What’s in my control? Your prep, mindset, and delivery are. The outcome? Not always. Letting go of what you can’t control frees up energy to focus where it counts.

The concept is echoed in Stoic Philosophy—a mental edge useful far beyond sport.

4. Use Rituals to Stay Grounded

Ever noticed how bowlers take a few deep breaths, adjust their wristbands, or follow a particular run-up routine? These aren’t quirks—they’re rituals. Rituals signal the brain that it’s time to perform—an essential part of managing workload under pressure.

Work Takeaway: Create your pre-performance routine. It could be reviewing your notes, listening to calming music, or doing breathwork. Psychologist Andrew Huberman has shown how such habits calm the nervous system and sharpen focus.

5. Debrief, Don’t Dwell

After the match, players debrief: What worked, what didn’t, and what to do better next time. The point? Progress over perfection.

Work Takeaway: After your big moment—whether a win or a stumble—reflect, but don’t ruminate. Capture the lessons and move forward. One bad delivery doesn’t define your game.

Final Over: Pressure Is a Privilege

To bowl in the final over is to be trusted in the pressure moment. In the same way, managing workload while leading big projects, closing deals, or representing your team means someone believes in your ability.

Cricketers show us that pressure is not something to fear—it’s something to manage, channel, and even thrive in.

So, when you’re next up to bowl—whether it’s with a ball or a business pitch—breathe in, trust your training, and deliver with purpose.

title: Confessions of a Social Media Manager: What It’s Really Like Behind the Posts
excerpt: I’ll start by admitting that I’m not a social media manager. Not at all. But I’ve ended up living in their world, avoiding content schedules, seeing real-time meme crises, and seeing flawless material undergo 19 rounds of changes because someone in legal “had a feeling.” They appear to have the ideal job from the outside. […]
content:
I’ll start by admitting that I’m not a social media manager. Not at all. But I’ve ended up living in their world, avoiding content schedules, seeing real-time meme crises, and seeing flawless material undergo 19 rounds of changes because someone in legal “had a feeling.”

They appear to have the ideal job from the outside. Posting clever one-liners, working from home while sipping coffee, and monitoring likes as if they were stocks. However, there is a level of pressure behind the promoted posts and carefully chosen content that I didn’t completely comprehend until I watched one (or five) in action.

The Mental Gymnastics at 3 AM

Do you believe that 5 PM is when their day ends? Try 3 a.m. They don’t sleep, and neither does Social. It’s a job that, often, runs in crisis mode, whether it’s putting out a brand fire, responding to a direct message that needs to be responded to in 20 minutes, or freaking out because someone unintentionally tweeted from the wrong account (again).

The Conflict Between Corporate and Creative

I’ve seen social media managers provide hilarious, amazing ideas that are diluted to the point of being as tasteless as toast. Guidelines for brand voice.

Approvals from stakeholders. “What if someone interprets it incorrectly?” Their work involves more than just coming up with brilliant ideas; it also involves being persistent enough to defend, edit, and occasionally bury them.

Everybody is a Critic

Everyone believes they know how to do social media better because of something about it. “What prevented you from posting about this trend?” “That hashtag is illogical.” “Is it possible for this to go viral?” They could fill a book—and not a small one—with the volume of unwanted advice they get every day.

But Additionally… The Magic Is in the Wins

From time to time, something emerges. A customer direct message becomes a brand love story, a post goes viral (on purpose), and the comments area evolves into a heartwarming hug fest. I’ve watched them light up—light up—after a viral post or a moment in the community that brought home to them why they do this. That fervor? It’s true.

So, no, I don’t manage social media. However, I greatly admire those who are. They are the cultural interpreters, the digital-first responders, and the people who make magic out of 280 characters and a popular song. Despite being behind the scenes, they are the brand’s true MVPs.

The next time you come upon the content you adore, perhaps leave a comment or a heart. You observed a social media manager there, and they’re letting out a little sigh of relief.

title: Customer Success Metrics That Matter in the New York Financial Sector
excerpt: The financial industry in New York is fast-paced and high-stakes, making client success more important than ever. To stay competitive, banks, asset managers, fintech firms, and providers of financial services need to have solid customer relationships. Nevertheless, providing value extends beyond acquiring new clients; maintaining long-term success necessitates monitoring the appropriate KPIs. The most important […]
content:
The financial industry in New York is fast-paced and high-stakes, making client success more important than ever. To stay competitive, banks, asset managers, fintech firms, and providers of financial services need to have solid customer relationships. Nevertheless, providing value extends beyond acquiring new clients; maintaining long-term success necessitates monitoring the appropriate KPIs. The most important customer success measures in New York’s financial scene are listed below.

How to Measure Customer Loyalty Using Net Promoter Score (NPS)

In the financial services industry, Net Promoter Score(NPS) is still one of the most accurate measures of client loyalty and satisfaction. Tracking NPS enables businesses to determine how probable it is that customers will promote their services to others, which is important in a competitive metropolis like New York where customers frequently have a variety of banking and investment options. In a business where reputation and trust are critical, a high NPS indicates that consumers are devoted advocates.

Customer Lifetime Value (CLV): Optimizing Profitability Over the Long Term

The total revenue a financial institution might anticipate from a single customer throughout their relationship is measured by the Customer Lifetime Value(CLV). In New York, where consumers frequently have intricated financial requirements, figuring out CLV is crucial to figuring out who the most valued clients are and how to customize services to increase long-term profitability. A high CLV suggests that a company’s offerings align with what customers want and need, which builds lasting relationships.

Reducing Churn in a Competitive Market with a High Customer Retention Rate

Because it costs a lot more to acquire new clients than it does to maintain current ones, customer retention is especially crucial in the financial industry. Customer Retention Rate calculates the proportion of clients a business maintains over a specific time frame. For established financial institutions, keeping up a strong retention rate is essential given the growth of fintech and digital banking options in New York. A poor rate of client retention is a warning sign that customers are looking for better deals or experiences elsewhere.

Time to Value (TTV): The Rate at Which Tangible Outcomes Are Delivered

The length of time it takes a client to recognize the value of your services is known as the Time To Value or TTV. In a city with as much speed as New York, clients want prompt and effective service. Shorter transaction times translate into happier customers, whether they are making a trade, applying for a loan, or opening a new investment account. It conveys the impression that your company is not just effective but also dedicated to assisting customers in quickly reaching their objectives.

Reducing Friction in the Customer Journey With the Customer Effort Score (CES)

Customers’ level of ease of interaction with your organization is measured by the Customer Effort Score(CES). In the financial industry of New York, where time is money, it is essential to minimize friction in the customer journey. A low CES indicates that users can swiftly and easily get the services they require via in-person meetings, mobile apps, or customer support channels.

Churn Rate: Calculating the Price of Client Loss

The percentage of clients who discontinue utilizing your services over a given time frame is measured by your churn rate. In New York’s financial industry, churn is a major problem because of competition from both traditional institutions and fintech companies. A high turnover rate frequently points to more serious issues, such as subpar customer service, unbeatable prices, or a dearth of tailored options.

First Contact Resolution (FCR): Improving Customer Assistance

A metric called First Call Resolution (FCR) gauges how well customer complaints are handled during the initial exchange with customer support. In the financial sector, where client satisfaction and trust can vary greatly, maintaining a high FCR is essential. Consumers anticipate prompt, precise, and helpful service, particularly when it comes to financial issues that have an immediate bearing on their investments and assets.

Conclusion

Customer success measurements are more than simply statistics in the high-stakes financial industry of New York; they are indicators of the health and future expansion of your company. Financial firms can create more robust and devoted customer connections by concentrating on indicators such as NPS, CLV, retention rates, and churn.

title: Customer Success Strategy: The Competitive Advantage Modern Corporations Can’t Ignore
excerpt: In today’s experience-driven economy, companies can no longer rely solely on acquiring new customers. Retaining and growing existing customers has become equally important for sustainable growth. This shift has pushed organizations to focus more on delivering consistent value after the sale. A well-defined customer success strategy helps businesses ensure that customers achieve their desired outcomes […]
content:
In today’s experience-driven economy, companies can no longer rely solely on acquiring new customers. Retaining and growing existing customers has become equally important for sustainable growth. This shift has pushed organizations to focus more on delivering consistent value after the sale.

A well-defined customer success strategy helps businesses ensure that customers achieve their desired outcomes while using their products or services. When customers succeed, they are more likely to remain loyal, expand their usage, and recommend the brand to others.

For modern corporations, customer success has evolved from a support function into a strategic driver of long-term business growth.

Understanding the Role of a Customer Success Strategy

A customer success strategy is a structured approach that organizations use to help customers achieve maximum value from their products or services. It focuses on proactive engagement rather than reactive support.

Instead of waiting for customers to report problems, companies actively guide them through onboarding, product adoption, and ongoing optimization. This proactive approach builds stronger relationships and helps businesses reduce churn while increasing customer satisfaction.

In highly competitive markets, companies that prioritize customer success often outperform those that focus only on sales and marketing.

Key Elements of an Effective Customer Success Strategy

A successful strategy involves several components that work together to improve the customer experience and business outcomes.

Customer Onboarding and Education

The first interaction after a purchase often determines the long-term success of the relationship. Effective onboarding ensures that customers understand how to use the product and achieve their goals quickly.

Educational resources, training programs, and guided product walkthroughs help customers gain confidence and maximize value early in their journey.

Proactive Customer Engagement

Successful organizations maintain regular communication with customers through check-ins, progress reviews, and personalized recommendations. This proactive engagement ensures that customers remain satisfied and continue to see value in the product or service.

A proactive approach is a fundamental part of any customer success strategy, as it helps organizations identify issues before they impact the customer experience.

Data-Driven Customer Insights

Modern businesses rely on data analytics to understand customer behavior, product usage, and engagement patterns. These insights help teams identify opportunities for improvement and personalize the customer experience.

Data-driven insights also allow companies to predict potential churn risks and take preventive action.

Cross-Department Collaboration

Customer success is not limited to one department. It requires collaboration across sales, marketing, product development, and customer support teams.

A unified customer success strategy ensures that every department works together to deliver consistent value and a seamless customer experience.

Benefits for Businesses and Customers

Organizations that invest in customer success initiatives gain several strategic advantages.

Increased Customer Retention

Satisfied customers are more likely to remain loyal to the brand, reducing churn and stabilizing revenue streams.

Higher Revenue Growth

Existing customers often generate additional revenue through renewals, upgrades, and cross-selling opportunities.

Stronger Brand Reputation

Companies known for prioritizing customer success build trust and credibility in the market.

Better Product Development

Customer feedback collected through success programs provides valuable insights that help companies improve products and services.

These benefits demonstrate why a strong customer success strategy has become essential for companies operating in competitive industries.

The Future of Customer Success in the Corporate World

As businesses continue to embrace digital transformation, customer expectations will continue to rise. Organizations must adopt proactive, data-driven approaches to deliver personalized experiences and long-term value.

Companies that develop a scalable customer success strategy will be better equipped to maintain customer loyalty, improve operational efficiency, and drive sustainable growth.

In the modern corporate environment, success is no longer defined only by the number of new customers acquired. Instead, it is measured by how effectively organizations help their customers succeed—and that is the true power of a well-executed customer success strategy.

title: Cybersecurity Trends Every Business Should Watch in 2024
excerpt: With technology always changing, cybersecurity is still a major worry for companies all around the world. The digital world is still growing as we go into 2024, offering opportunities and challenges to businesses of all kinds. It is critical to stay up to date on the latest trends and developments in cyber threats to protect […]
content:
With technology always changing, cybersecurity is still a major worry for companies all around the world. The digital world is still growing as we go into 2024, offering opportunities and challenges to businesses of all kinds. It is critical to stay up to date on the latest trends and developments in cyber threats to protect sensitive data and ensure continuous operations. Cyber threats are getting increasingly complex.

Zero-Trust Structure

In 2024 Zero-trust architecture (ZTA) will remain at the center of cybersecurity developments as companies emphasize risk reduction and data protection in an ever-complex threat scenario.
These are some big trends that all businesses need to be aware of.

Combination of AI and Machine Learning: To improve threat detection and response capabilities, AI and machine learning are being included in zero-trust frameworks.

Cloud Platforms Should Have Zero Trust: Zero trust concepts are being used in cloud environments to safeguard information and software managed externally due to the increasing adoption of cloud services.

Privacy-Centric Security: With Zero trust architecture, safeguarding data at an individual level is becoming more important.

The Ascent of Quantum Information

The field of cybersecurity is changing as quantum computing develops.
In 2024, businesses should be aware of the following trends.

Preparedness for Post-Quantum Era: Organizations must evaluate their preparedness to fend off potential quantum threats as quantum computing advances.

Intelligence on Quantum Threats: Businesses must invest in quantum threat intelligence to keep ahead of possible attacks because of the development of quantum capabilities in both insensitive and preventive cybersecurity tactics.

Regulatory Factors to Consider: Regulations about cybersecurity may start to be established by authorities because of the new issues that quantum computing presents.

Problems With Cloud Security

Cloud security is still a major worry for companies in 2024 as they manage a cyber threat scenario that is getting more complicated.
The following are some cloud security-related cybersecurity developments that companies should be aware of.

Multi-Cloud Security: Content and software security across many clouds becomes critical as enterprises adopt multi-cloud systems to take advantage of the finest services from various providers.

Serverless Security: Although serverless computing is more economical and scalable, it also brings with it special security issues.

Investigating and Identifying Potential Threats: To detect and lessen new cyber threats, proactive threat data collection and surveillance of threats are crucial.

Conclusion

A proactive strategy for cybersecurity that includes human development, technology innovation, legal compliance, and risk-minimizing methods is necessary to navigate the digital frontier. Businesses may strengthen their defenses against cyber-attacks and protect their assets in an increasingly connected environment by being alert and adjusting to evolving trends.

title: Digital Marketing: Strategies to Boost Business
excerpt: Having a strong online presence is a must for businesses. Digital marketing strategies play a pivotal role in achieving this goal. It enables businesses to connect with their target audience, build brand awareness, and drive conversions. Let’s delve into some of the top digital marketing strategies and how they can help businesses succeed in the […]
content:
Having a strong online presence is a must for businesses. Digital marketing strategies play a pivotal role in achieving this goal. It enables businesses to connect with their target audience, build brand awareness, and drive conversions.

Let’s delve into some of the top digital marketing strategies and how they can help businesses succeed in the digital realm.

Search Engine Optimization (SEO)

SEO is a cornerstone of digital marketing, focusing on optimizing a website to rank higher in Search Engine Results Pages (SERPs). By optimizing website content, keywords, and meta tags, businesses can improve their visibility and attract more organic traffic. Effective SEO strategies involve keyword research, on-page optimization, and building high-quality backlinks to enhance authority and credibility.

Content Marketing

Content marketing involves creating and distributing valuable, relevant content to attract and engage target audiences. From blog posts and articles to videos and infographics, compelling content helps businesses establish thought leadership, build trust with consumers, and drive website traffic. Content marketing also plays a crucial role in SEO, as fresh, high-quality content is favored by search engine algorithms.

Social Media Marketing

Social media platforms offer powerful tools for businesses to connect with their audience, build relationships, and promote products or services. Through strategic social media marketing, businesses can engage with followers, drive website traffic, and generate leads. Effective social media strategies involve identifying the right platforms for the target audience, creating engaging content, and leveraging paid advertising to reach specific demographics.

Email Marketing

Email marketing remains one of the most effective channels for nurturing leads, driving sales, and fostering customer loyalty. By segmenting email lists, personalizing content, and automating campaigns, businesses can deliver targeted messages to subscribers, driving engagement and conversions. Email marketing is also highly measurable, allowing businesses to track open rates, click-through rates, and other key metrics to optimize campaign performance.

Pay-Per-Click (PPC) Advertising

PPC advertising enables businesses to reach their target audience through paid ads displayed on search engines and social media platforms. By bidding on relevant keywords and targeting specific demographics, businesses can drive targeted traffic to their website and increase conversions. PPC advertising offers precise targeting options and instant visibility, making it an effective strategy for driving immediate results.

Conclusion

An effective digital marketing strategy empowers businesses to maximize their online presence, reach their target audience, and drive growth. By leveraging these top digital marketing strategies, businesses can stay ahead of the competition and achieve their marketing objectives.

title: Don’t Let Tech Mistakes Write Your Business Story: 4 Fixes That Save Time and Money
excerpt: Technology should feel like your favourite sidekick, not the villain stealing the limelight. But all too often, tech missteps can hijack your business narrative. Let’s nip four common fixes in the bud to save time and money, avoid budget leaks, and keep your reputation intact. 1. Skip the Antivirus See What Happens It sounds obvious, […]
content:
Technology should feel like your favourite sidekick, not the villain stealing the limelight. But all too often, tech missteps can hijack your business narrative. Let’s nip four common fixes in the bud to save time and money, avoid budget leaks, and keep your reputation intact.

1. Skip the Antivirus See What Happens

It sounds obvious, but some small businesses treat antivirus protection like optional decor. Cutting corners there can backfire, literally. You might risk malware, ransomware, or data breaches that spiral into costly legal entanglements. Yes, one cyber incident is enough to derail your business.

Fix it: Invest in reliable, preferably cloud-based, antivirus software. Many effective options are free or low-cost, and the peace of mind is priceless.

2. Don’t Skip Updates and Ignored Trends

Hanging onto outdated software may feel cosy, but it’s essentially a ticking time bomb. Ignoring updates or being oblivious to new tech trends not only makes you inefficient, vulnerable, and less competitive, but also prevents you from finding smarter ways to save time and money.

Fix it: Enable automatic system updates and stay curious. Dedicate just five minutes a day to scan tech news or blogs (like Inc.). You’ll stay agile and maybe spot your next growth hack.

3. Let Your Phone Be a Security Sieve

A phone isn’t just personal; it’s a key to your business vault. Losing it, especially when it’s unlocked, invites hackers, scams, and leaked credentials.

Fix it: Always lock your device. Use strong screen protection and enable remote tracking or wiping. Small step. Huge difference.

4. Overlooking Privacy Policies Is Like Skipping the Fine Print on a Loan

That long wall of text at the bottom of a website? It’s not bedtime reading, but maybe it should be. Blindly handing over your data, or your clients’ data, can be a legal landmine, especially in the cloud storage era. Taking a closer look now can help you save time and money later.

Fix it: Skim privacy policies. Focus on data ownership, transfer rights, and usage clauses. If unsure, consult someone who understands legal lingo.

Why These Fixes Actually Save Money

Prevention over Cleanup: Fixing a hacked system costs way more than the few bucks for antivirus software; old-school logic preserved.

Efficiency Adds Up: Auto-updates and improved tech avoid slowdowns and manual headaches.

Trust Is Currency: A single data breach or misstep can cost you hard-earned client trust, and their wallets.

Final Thought

Imagine your business narrative: Is tech steering the ship, or crashing your story? With these four fixes, you regain the pen, save time and money, and keep the plot exactly where you want it: in your hands.

title: Edge Computing for Business: Processing Data Where It Matters Most
excerpt: Companies today generate massive amounts of data every second. Traditional cloud systems send all that data to distant servers for processing, but what if your business could analyze information right where it is created? That is exactly what edge computing for business does, and it is changing how companies operate in 2025. What Makes Edge […]
content:
Companies today generate massive amounts of data every second. Traditional cloud systems send all that data to distant servers for processing, but what if your business could analyze information right where it is created? That is exactly what edge computing for business does, and it is changing how companies operate in 2025.

What Makes Edge Computing Different

Edge computing for business brings data processing closer to the source instead of relying on faraway data centers. Think of a retail store with security cameras. Rather than sending hours of video footage to the cloud for analysis, edge computing allows the camera itself to process that data instantly and flag only important events. This approach saves time, reduces costs, and delivers faster insights that businesses can act on immediately.

Why Businesses Choose Edge Computing

Speed matters in modern business. Edge computing reduces latency to under five milliseconds, which means your systems can respond almost instantly. Autonomous vehicles, smart healthcare devices, and manufacturing equipment all need this kind of split-second decision making to function safely and effectively.

Security also improves with edge computing for business solutions. When data stays local instead of traveling across networks to central servers, there are fewer opportunities for hackers to intercept it. Companies handling sensitive customer information or operating in regulated industries find this localized approach helps them meet compliance requirements more easily.

Applications of Edge Computing for Business

Manufacturing plants use edge computing to monitor equipment in real time and predict when machines need maintenance before they break down. Retailers deploy edge solutions to track inventory instantly and analyze customer behavior patterns without delay. Healthcare providers rely on edge computing to process patient data from monitoring devices and enable faster diagnoses.

The integration of artificial intelligence with edge computing for business is creating even more possibilities. Smart devices can now perform complex tasks like video analysis and anomaly detection without constant cloud connectivity, making operations more reliable especially in remote locations with limited internet access.

As more connected devices enter workplaces and the demand for instant insights grows, edge computing for business will continue expanding across industries. Companies that embrace this approach now position themselves to operate faster, smarter, and more efficiently than competitors still relying solely on traditional cloud computing models.

title: Tech Solutions That Ensure Employees’ Safety
excerpt: With employees returning to offices, organizations across are embracing tech solutions that ensure employees’ safety in this COVID-19 era.
content:
With employees returning to offices amid the global-health crisis, organizations worldwide are embracing high-tech personal protection measures to keep their workforce safe. New apps, gadgets, and wearable devices are helping employers with tasks like electronic contact tracing and taking temperatures. For instance: Few wearable devices beep when two people come within six feet of each other. Thereby, creating a high-tech force field to remind people to abide by social distancing guidelines. Now, let’s look into the different tech solutions that ensure employees’ safety in this COVID-19 struck world.

Here are a few tech solutions that ensure employees’ safety

Prescreening App

Many organizations today are investing in prescreening apps that employees need to download on their phones.  The logic of this app is simple – to screen the activities of an employee even before he/she can come to the office. For instance, even before going to the office, the employee needs to punch in his/her present temperatures and activities they participated in over the past 2 weeks, like dining out, etc. Depending on the risk factors, the employee will get a message like,

  • Cleared to come in
  • Stay home and check the next day, or
  • Contact your physician

HR leaders believe this is one of the best measures to contain the spread of COVID-19 in the workplace. However, the only drawback of this app is that it relies on the data that the employees provide – which can either be accurate or not.

Temperature Monitoring App/Device

Domo, a cloud-based software company in Utah has come up with an entire suite of “Get Back to Work” apps, including one that allows employees to record their temperature at home and then again at the entrance of the workplace. Not just that it also offers a Safe Worker App, which you can use to communicate directly with your employees. Likewise, there are many temperature monitoring devices available in the market today. And many organizations are using these devices on a  primary basis to monitor the spread of Coronavirus and keep their workforce safe.

AI-Powered Thermal Cameras

AI-enabled detection cameras are capable of conducting mass screening and provides real-time updates of an individual’s body temperature. For instance, the AI Fever Detection Camera from IN Depth offers quick and accurate detection of elevated body temperatures. In other words, the IN Depth AI-powered thermal cameras leverage highly advanced artificial intelligence and scene analytics for real-time detection and assessments of elevated human body temperature.

Contact Tracing App

Contact tracing apps are a boon to all HR professionals. Here’s why – it might take an HR professional nearly 15 hours to make a single trace, whereas a contact tracing app can do the same in just 15 seconds. 

Companies today are buying electronic tracing apps and wearable devices as a measure to keep their employees safe. Did you know? Pricewaterhouse Cooper (PwC) has sold the contact tracing app called “Check In” to more than 60 companies now! 

The contact tracing app basically tracks the employees’ time, distance, and frequency of contact with co-workers. It also alerts each employee of his or her risk level with a proximity score. And employers can use these proximity scores to determine who should stay at home, who should get tested, etc. However, the app only works on company property. So, to help employers track employees who work in warehouses or factories where they don’t carry phones, PwC is unveiling a lanyard with a tracker. This value addition has made HR officials stress-free who were previously overwhelmed with the nonstop job of contact tracing. 

Other Technological Innovations

Every day, people are working on different innovations to make life simpler. And most importantly to contain the spread of COVID-19. Kenzen, a New York city-based company, makes wearable devices that track physiological changes to keep employees safe from heat and overexertion. The good news is, it may expand its service into early illness detection next year. Also, the company is in talks with large corporations about the possibility as it works to address worker privacy concerns. 

In addition, companies such as Wigle Whiskey, a Pittsburgh-based microdistillery, have introduced technology such as air filtration systems to keep the employees safe. Likewise, there are many technological innovations in the making intended to prevent the spread of COVID-19 and monitor the existing cases effectively!

Final Thoughts

Only relying on tech solutions won’t help! Companies need to educate their employees on safety and hygiene measures. Sanitize the entire building on a daily basis. Also, ensure employees wear masks (at least while interacting with others) and maintain social distance at all times. Let’s fight COVID-19 in unison, and practice safety and hygiene measures to keep ourselves and our loved ones safe!
